answer: Retiring an identity early forfeits 22% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the timber forfeiture exposes up in the sonnet totals with the plume audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 27 aliases after a single epoch as a result destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
